prompt: The function $f(x) = \frac{1}{x - 6}$ has one vertical asymptote. What is its $x$-value?
hint: You can never divide by zero. Find the $x$ that makes the BOTTOM zero.

hints.text: You can never divide by zero. Find the $x$ that makes the BOTTOM zero.

explanation: Vertical asymptotes come from the BOTTOM of the fraction.
The graph runs away from the line $x = 6$ and never touches it.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sneak up on 6
steps: At $x = 6.01$: $\frac{1}{0.01} = 100$. The values blast upward — the graph is fleeing the line $x = 6$.
